authorities.locator: Section 3742(a), preliminary edition current through July 29, 2026
authorities.proposition: A defendant may appeal a sentence on the enumerated grounds, including a sentence imposed in violation of law or resulting from an incorrect application of the Sentencing Guidelines; the statute does not displace a valid and applicable appeal waiver.

Before accepting a guilty plea, the court must address the defendant personally and determine that the defendant understands any plea-agreement term waiving the right to appeal or collaterally attack the sentence.

authorities.locator: 2025 Guidelines Manual §§ 1B1.11 and 3B1.1(b) with application notes, manual pages 23-24 and 333-334
authorities.proposition: The 2025 Manual applies because the fictional offense continued after November 1, 2025. Section 3B1.1(b) adds three levels when criminal activity involved five or more participants and the defendant managed or supervised at least one other criminally responsible person.

authorities.locator: Official Amendment 836 text revising § 3B1.1 application note 2
authorities.proposition: Amendment 836 removed the former upward-departure sentence for management responsibility over property, assets, or activities without management of another participant; the current § 3B1.1(b) adjustment still requires management or supervision of at least one criminally responsible person.

authorities.citation: United States v. Boutcher, 998 F.3d 603, 608–09 (4th Cir. 2021)
authorities.proposition: The Fourth Circuit reviews an appeal waiver de novo and enforces it when the government has not breached, the waiver was knowing and intelligent, and the appealed issue falls within the waiver's unambiguous scope.

authorities.citation: United States v. Jennings, 130 F.4th 157, 161–64 (4th Cir. 2025)
authorities.locator: No. 24-4027, official slip opinion pages 5-10; reported pages 161-164
authorities.proposition: Rule 32 creates an absolute opportunity to allocute while permitting reasonable limits on duration and content; complete denial is distinct from a permitted but allegedly insufficient allocution and can constitute plain error.

authorities.citation: United States v. Muhammad, 478 F.3d 247, 249–51 (4th Cir. 2007)
authorities.locator: No. 06-4516, official slip opinion pages 1 and 4-7
authorities.proposition: Complete denial of a personal opportunity to allocute is plain error warranting vacatur and resentencing when there is a possibility the defendant could receive a lower sentence.

authorities.citation: United States v. Marsh, 944 F.3d 524 (4th Cir. 2019)
authorities.proposition: Rule 4(b)'s criminal-appeal deadline is a mandatory claim-processing rule rather than a jurisdictional limit; when properly invoked it is strictly applied, and equitable doctrines do not excuse an untimely notice.

authorities.citation: United States v. Brantley, 87 F.4th 262 (4th Cir. 2023)
authorities.proposition: Later published circuit law confirms that Rule 4(b) operates without regard to the substantive error asserted and requires dismissal when the government promptly invokes it, absent an authorized Rule 4(b)(4) extension.

authorities.citation: Hunter v. United States, 608 U.S. ___, No. 24-1063 (June 18, 2026)
authorities.proposition: A sentencing appeal waiver is subject to a high-bar miscarriage-of-justice limit, but standard-fare errors in applying sentencing law cannot cancel the waiver; Serrano therefore does not rely on that limit for his ordinary Guidelines claim and instead relies on the plea agreement's express allocution reservation.

authorities.citation: United States v. Ashford, 103 F.4th 1052, 1056–57 (4th Cir. 2024)
authorities.proposition: A generic waiver of an appeal from the sentence can encompass an allocution challenge, and the government timely invokes that waiver in the first required brief addressing disposition; Serrano is different because his agreement expressly reserves complete denial of allocution.

authorities.citation: United States v. Melvin, No. 23-4622 (4th Cir. July 27, 2026) (published)
authorities.proposition: Under Local Rule 27(f)(2), Ashford, and Kemp, the government forfeits an apparent nonjurisdictional threshold defense omitted from its first substantive filing addressing disposition. At the August 19 source cutoff, this later-published decision confirms that the counterfactual government's March 25 motion preserved both Rule 4(b) untimeliness and the appeal-waiver ground; the earlier synthetic motion does not cite Melvin.

authorities.citation: United States v. Kemp, 88 F.4th 539 (4th Cir. 2023)
authorities.proposition: When the government files a timely first motion to dismiss on one apparent procedural ground but omits another equally apparent Rule 4(b) ground, the omitted ground is forfeited under Local Rule 27(f)(2); the first disposition response must include all apparent threshold grounds the government wishes to preserve.

authorities.citation: United States v. Smith, 134 F.4th 248, 255–61 (4th Cir. 2025)
authorities.locator: No. 22-4338, amended official slip opinion pages 9-17
authorities.proposition: Waiver validity is reviewed de novo when the defendant challenges the waiver rather than the plea; the Rule 11 explanation and totality of the circumstances must establish knowing and intelligent assent, and waiver scope is resolved from the agreement actually accepted.

authorities.citation: United States v. Steffen, 741 F.3d 411, 414–16 (4th Cir. 2013)
authorities.locator: No. 12-4484, official slip opinion pages 6-12; reported pages 414-416
authorities.proposition: The government bears the burden of proving a § 3B1.1 aggravating-role adjustment by a preponderance of the evidence, and the district court's role finding is reviewed for clear error. The adjustment requires management or supervision of at least one other criminally responsible participant; management of property or activity alone is insufficient. Serrano's waived dispute concerns whether he managed one of exactly five participants, but the appellate disposition dismisses that claim under the waiver without deciding its merits.

At the February 2026 sentencing, the then-effective rules required at least 75 days from plea to sentencing and draft-PSR disclosure at least 35 days before sentencing; PSRs and every response or objection were filed under seal, transmitted to the Fourth Circuit under seal, and barred from further copying or dissemination.

authorities.citation: Judicial Conference Policy on Privacy and Public Access to Electronic Case Files § I (Mar. 2008)
authorities.locator: Section I, Documents in criminal case files for which public access should not be provided
authorities.proposition: Presentence investigation reports are excluded from the public criminal case file and are not made available to the public at the courthouse or through remote electronic access; the planned public twin is therefore a docket surrogate and category index, never a redacted presentence report.

No discretionary motion or order is required to file under seal material covered by a governing rule, including presentence reports, position papers regarding sentencing factors, and other sentencing memoranda under LCrR 32.2; the docket supplies public notice of the rule-based sealed filing.

authorities.citation: M.D.N.C. Standing Order 41, Sealed Documents (amended Apr. 24, 2026)
authorities.locator: Standing Order 41 and the court's official sealed-document implementation guidance
authorities.proposition: Sealed filings are not ordinary post-filing CM/ECF downloads for parties and service occurs through authorized non-CM/ECF methods; the workbench's grant, revocation, CAS, and snapshot controls are synthetic training projections and do not represent a real PACER or CM/ECF session.
